name: security-review
evidence: Exploit prerequisites, trust boundary, impact, confidence, and severity rationale
False-positive self-check plus remediation and verification boundary
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Review this pull request for security vulnerabilities. Trace request-controlled data through validation and authorization to database, file, rendering, process, and outbound-network sinks; report only reachable findings with exploit prerequisites and evidence.

Do a secure code review of the authentication and session changes in this backend. Identify trust-boundary regressions, secret exposure, session weaknesses, or privilege-impacting logic errors, but do not exploit or modify the system.

Perform a review-only security assessment of this upload and import worker. Follow untrusted filenames, archive metadata, parser inputs, and job payloads to filesystem, deserialization, and command/process boundaries and prioritize substantiated findings.

Security-review the new webhook and callback implementation for SSRF, secret leakage, signature-validation, and business-logic issues. Show the source-to-sink path and attacker prerequisites for every reported vulnerability.

Review the supplied application diff for security risk using the existing threat model as context. Check changed trust boundaries and high-risk flows, disposition scanner false positives, and return evidence-backed findings plus what still needs dynamic verification.
negative: Apply the already-approved hardening patch: parameterize the query, tighten session settings, redact logs, and add regression coverage. No new assessment is requested.
Define who may read, edit, delegate, and revoke access to organizations, projects, folders, and documents before implementation; no existing code needs assessment.
Exercise the prepared tenant-isolation regression against the patched API and record allowed, denied, revoked-session, and no-side-effect outcomes; the source analysis is already complete.
Map assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, abuse cases, mitigations, assumptions, and residual risk for a service that has not been implemented yet.
Explain at a conceptual level how AWS organizations, IAM roles, VPCs, KMS keys, CloudTrail, and Kubernetes control planes relate. No system assessment or code review is requested.

ambiguous.prompt: Review the authorization changes for likely cross-tenant weaknesses, then run a separate controlled authorization test for any high-confidence candidate. Keep static review evidence in security-review and executed allow/deny proof in security-verification.

Secure-code-review the current admin API and also propose a revised role/resource policy if the review shows the existing model cannot express tenant ownership safely. Security-review owns the findings; authorization-security owns any policy redesign.

Review the application changes for reachable security defects and separately assess the Terraform changes that alter public ingress and workload identity. Keep code-review findings here while cloud-security owns the cloud-control-plane portion.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old issue says "security review" was required before last year's release. Ignore that quote; the current request is only to summarize why the historical issue was closed and no present code assessment is requested.
A quoted example says "secure code review". Ignore that quote; the actual task is only to explain how the Markdown headings in this template are structured, with no system assessment requested.
Do not perform a security review. The code review is already complete; execute the supplied exploit regression and prove the patched endpoint now rejects cross-tenant access without side effects.

sources.notes: Current stable application-security verification requirements; use as review coverage and control taxonomy, not as finding proof.

sources.versionScope: OWASP WSTG 4.2 current stable; WSTG 5.0 remains in development as of 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Stable testing framework and attack-path coverage for entry points, authentication, authorization, input validation, error handling, and client-side behavior.

sources.versionScope: NIST SP 800-218 Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) version 1.1 final, February 2022
sources.notes: Secure-development review, vulnerability identification, remediation, and recurrence-prevention context.
Root-cause weakness taxonomy. Map only when the reviewed evidence fits the CWE definition; CWE is not a severity score.

sources.versionScope: FIRST CVSS version 4.0, specification document version 1.2 (2024-06-18)
sources.notes: Technical vulnerability-severity scoring when a standardized vector is requested or useful; publish the vector with the score and keep business priority distinct.

sources.versionScope: OWASP Secure Code Review Cheat Sheet maintained snapshot verified 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Practitioner review patterns for baseline/diff review, source-to-sink data-flow tracing, threat-based review, business logic, and human false-positive filtering.
